body.statement: Fix a successful certificate \(\lambda\). In the saturated multinomial model on \(S\), \(\phi_P\) is the efficient influence function of \(F_{\lambda}(P)\). Under independent multinomial sampling, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{S,\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\), \(\sqrt N\{\widehat\tau_N-F_{\lambda}(P)\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{k=1}^N\phi_P(O_k)+o_P(1)\), the studentized statistic converges uniformly to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the plug-in variance \(\sum_{s\in S}\widehat P_N(s)\phi_{\widehat P_N}(s)^2\) is uniformly consistent. On the compatible submodel this gives Wald inference for \(\tau_{x,y}\).
body.justification: A complete symbolic identifier becomes statistically usable once its rational output has face-tangent inference.
body.gap: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive graph-native influence functions for important functional classes, but not for arbitrary rational outputs created by exact-support identification on a lower-dimensional multinomial face.
body.consumer: Analysts with known structural zeros obtain standard errors and confidence intervals without replacing the deterministic intervention target.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(d=|S|\), and regard the simplex as a subset of \(\mathbb R^d\).  On
\[
K_\epsilon=\left\{p\in\Delta(S):\min_{s\in S}p(s)\ge\epsilon\right\},
\]
every supported prefix probability is at least \(\epsilon\): for a prefix \(w\in S^{\le i-1}\), choose an extending cell \(s\in S\) and use \(p(V_{<i}=w)\ge p(s)\).  The rational representation in the rational-functional theorem therefore has denominators uniformly bounded away from zero on a relative neighborhood of \(K_\epsilon\).  Since the dimension is finite, \(F_\lambda\) has uniformly bounded first and second derivatives on a slightly larger compact neighborhood, for example wherever all cell probabilities are at least \(\epsilon/2\).

Write
\[
g_P(s)=\frac{\partial F_\lambda(P)}{\partial P(s)}.
\]
The definition of \(\phi_P\) gives \(\phi_P(s)=g_P(s)-\sum_uP(u)g_P(u)\), and hence \(\sum_sP(s)\phi_P(s)=0\).  If \(a:S\to\mathbb R\) is any score in the saturated multinomial tangent space, so that \(\sum_sP(s)a(s)=0\), the path \(P_t(s)=P(s)\{1+t a(s)\}\) satisfies
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}F_\lambda(P_t)\right|_{t=0}
=\sum_s g_P(s)P(s)a(s)
=\sum_s\phi_P(s)P(s)a(s).                                     \tag{31}
\]
Every mean-zero function on \(S\) is such a tangent direction.  Thus \(\phi_P\) is the unique mean-zero representer of all pathwise derivatives in the saturated multinomial tangent space, and hence is the efficient influence function.  Its variance is \(\sigma^2(P)\) by definition.

Let
\[
E_N=\left\{\|\widehat P_N-P\|_\infty\le\epsilon/2\right\}.
\]
The multinomial variance formula and a union bound with Chebyshev's inequality give
\[
\sup_{P\in K_\epsilon}P(E_N^c)
\le \frac{4d}{N\epsilon^2}.                                   \tag{32}
\]
Moreover, the event that some supported cell is unobserved has probability at most
\[
\sum_{s\in S}\{1-P(s)\}^N\le d e^{-N\epsilon}.                \tag{33}
\]
On its complement, \(D_S(\widehat P_N)>0\), so the plug-in definition equals \(F_\lambda(\widehat P_N)\).  On \(E_N\), the uniform second-derivative bound and Taylor's theorem give
\[
F_\lambda(\widehat P_N)-F_\lambda(P)
=\sum_{s\in S}g_P(s)\{\widehat P_N(s)-P(s)\}+R_N,
\qquad
|R_N|\le C\|\widehat P_N-P\|_2^2,                             \tag{34}
\]
where \(C\) is independent of \(P\in K_\epsilon\).  Because the empirical masses sum to one, the linear term in (34) is
\[
\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\phi_P(O_k).                               \tag{35}
\]
Also \(\sup_P E_P[N\|\widehat P_N-P\|_2^2]\le d\), so (32)--(34) imply \(\sqrt N R_N=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  Together with (33), this proves the asserted uniform asymptotic linear expansion for \(\widehat\tau_N\).

On \(\mathcal P_{S,\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\), bounded first derivatives and \(\sigma(P)\ge\underline\sigma\) imply a constant \(M<\infty\) such that
\[
\left|\frac{\phi_P(s)}{\sigma(P)}\right|\le M
\quad\text{for all }s\in S
\quad\text{and all }P\in\mathcal P_{S,\epsilon,\underline\sigma}. \tag{36}
\]
For any sequence \(P_N\) in this class, the triangular array
\[
W_{N,k}=\frac{\phi_{P_N}(O_k)}{\sqrt N\,\sigma(P_N)},
\qquad k=1,\ldots,N,
\]
has independent mean-zero entries, total variance one, and satisfies the Lindeberg condition by (36).  The cited Lindeberg--Feller theorem therefore gives
\[
\frac1{\sqrt N\,\sigma(P_N)}\sum_{k=1}^N\phi_{P_N}(O_k)
\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).                              \tag{37}
\]
If convergence in (37) were not uniform over the class, a violating sequence \(P_N\) could be selected, contradicting (37).  Hence the convergence is uniform.

Define \(v(p)=\sum_sp(s)\phi_p(s)^2\) wherever the prefix denominators are positive.  The same compact-neighborhood derivative bounds make \(v\) uniformly continuous near \(K_\epsilon\).  Equations (32)--(33) and uniform consistency of \(\widehat P_N\) consequently imply
\[
\sum_{s\in S}\widehat P_N(s)\phi_{\widehat P_N}(s)^2
-\sigma^2(P)=o_P(1)                                            \tag{38}
\]
uniformly, on the event where the displayed plug-in expression is defined; defining it arbitrarily on the complement does not change (38) because that complement has uniformly vanishing probability by (33).  The variance lower bound and (38), followed by the uniform version of Slutsky's argument, turn (34)--(37) into uniform convergence of
\[
\frac{\sqrt N\{\widehat\tau_N-F_\lambda(P)\}}
{\left\{\sum_s\widehat P_N(s)\phi_{\widehat P_N}(s)^2\right\}^{1/2}}
\]
to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Finally, on the compatible submodel, the rational-functional theorem gives \(F_\lambda(P_\theta)=\tau_{x,y}(\theta)\), so the same expansion and studentization provide Wald inference for the causal target rather than merely for an observed-law functional.
